regions.full_page: before reaching Albany. Then down the Hudson to Garrison just across from Westpoint Military Academy. Walking to the Monastery about a mile below, I said holy Mass close to 9 a.m. Deo Gratias! I found things so inviting afterwords that I decided to rest there a day. The grounds are spacious to say the least and I might say almost dangerously grand. Originally there were, I believe over 400 acres. They soled quit a piece of it includ- ing the Sugar-loaf Mountain - one of the most beautiful along the Hudson, to help defray building of the new Monastery. After vespers I went for a hyke. Only half determined to climb the Mt., and feeling more like myself in the holy habit I just went as I was. How- ever, the air was so salubrious as I ascended and the breezes and shade so inviting that I pushed on and up through under brush and across paths and roads till I found none of these any more. Finally, after quite a climb through almost trackless brush, mostly not dense, I reached the rather unin- viting top and climbed a gentle evergreen to look out over the canoy (canopy) of sumit foliage. The scenry was grand, as far as it went, but in remembrance of the beautiful views, decade age so familiar to us, from Mt. Saint Helen and before that from the gentler hills of old Trimbelle, I soon found it monotnous and disapointing in hoped-for views. So I climed down after a little and started down the face of old Sugar-loaf. I think it was a totally unexplored route; but aided by a strong emergency staff, and dreamings of similar climb- ings - though on smaller scales - 60 or more years ago, I made the descent with some narow escapes and a few harmless bumps on rear fenders. Deo Gratias. It was close to supper-time when I got back to the monastery, and I need not tell you I had an appetite. We had recreation that evening which ... very happy and its a long time since I slept sounder than that night. Next day, finding he had some extra business in New York, Fr. Guardian brought me down by auto. We crossed over between Sugar-loaf and the now famous Mt. of Atonement and went down over the High-lands. It was quite a: descent indeed. After we had gone down so many hills that I was beginning to think we were coming close to normally level ground we suddenly curved past a sign: "Hill". I had to smile as we dashed past it and over the top, the dri- ver seemingly knowing every inch and bump ahead till again and again we con- tinued to make inclines. At about 11 a.m. we passed through picturesque old Yonkers and still down with, few little ups. Via the Western Driveway past the Washington Bridge (over the Hudson), and over Canal Street past "Office of the Irish World" we reached Our Lady of Sorrows Monastery just before the noon Angelus and dinner greeting.
